minutes.headline: Finance Committee set warrant recommendations but held its override vote for the full board
minutes.summary: The Finance Committee worked through the annual town meeting warrant article by article, recommending approval or no-financial-impact findings on most housekeeping, revolving-fund, capital and enterprise-fund articles, while deferring items still missing final numbers (FY26 closeouts, FY27 omnibus budget, PEG enterprise fund, three union contracts still in negotiation, and prior-year bills). The committee split on a new health-insurance stabilization transfer and on a new Assistant Town Manager/HR Director grade, and it postponed voting on its recommendation for the Proposition 2½ override so the full five-member board, including two absent members, could weigh in before the mailing deadline.

budget_items.what_was_said: A new revolving fund would let the economic development committee handle sponsorship money for events like the meet-and-greet without it passing through the town's general accounts. FY2027 spending cap discussed.

Spending limits were read for ambulance billing, timber rights, school custodial special details, Green Thumb, library, Council on Aging, storm water task force, electric/gas/plumbing inspector, technology, wetlands protection fees, COA meal site, and parks programming revolving funds.
Two outstanding invoices to Aeroseptic were named as the only known prior-year bills so far; recommendation deferred to town meeting since more may surface.

budget_items.topic: FY26 closeout / snow and ice deficit
budget_items.what_was_said: The current estimated operating deficit, driven mostly by snow and ice removal, was given; transfers will cover part of it and up to a stated amount was earmarked from free cash pending final snow and ice bills.
Two override tiers would go to voters as separate ballot questions, with only the highest approved amount implemented; the Finance Committee deferred taking a position pending the full board.

An accounting error had moved the same unspent FY23 capital funds through two prior votes (TCP roof repair, then FY26 capital); this article unwinds both so the money returns to the FY26 capital plan cleanly.

Individual capital items were read out including DPW bridge completion, a police cruiser, a fire engine/brush truck, primary school entry/driveway and playground design, public safety building roof and boiler work, door security intercoms at Turkey Hill and the primary school, and a DPW front-end loader.
The planned motion would transfer this amount from solid waste enterprise revenue to operate the program for FY2027; the fund does not cover recycling costs.
The fund would use enterprise revenue to pay Fitchburg for water and recoup a percentage under an intermunicipal agreement; figures were based on usage estimates.
A transfer toward the sewer enterprise's share of retiree health benefit liability; a member asked why the PEG/PAC enterprise carries no similar contribution.
Total FY2027 operating budget figure for the sewer enterprise fund.

budget_items.topic: SAP salary schedule / cost of living adjustment
budget_items.what_was_said: A cost-of-living increase for non-union salaried employees would be funded from the salary reserve; a member clarified it is not tied to any federal COLA figure.

budget_items.topic: Special appropriation: TC Pasio and assessor position
budget_items.what_was_said: Funds requested for TC Pasio operating and decommissioning costs and for a special assistant to the assessor position.

budget_items.topic: Free cash to OPEB trust fund
budget_items.what_was_said: Ten percent of certified free cash was described as being transferred to the OPEB trust under the town's financial policy.
A second consecutive year of a small deposit was proposed to build a cushion against retirement buyout costs exceeding the operating budget line.
Funds requested for activities marking the town's 300th anniversary; some members felt the amount was too large given past reliance on volunteers.
A standard annual transfer from free cash to the general-purpose stabilization fund, distinct from the vehicle/special purpose fund.

A new deposit was proposed as a cushion against a future spike in health insurance costs; total town and school insurance costs across active and retiree accounts were estimated. One member asked for defined trigger criteria for using the fund before supporting it.

budget_items.topic: Vacation accrual system transition liability buyout
budget_items.what_was_said: The town proposed buying out the full accrued-vacation liability at current dollar value ahead of a transition to a continuous accrual system, covering SAP employees and settled/near-settled union groups.
A member recalled roughly this figure as the cost of printing and mailing full warrant booklets to every household, cited in favor of switching to a postcard notice.

Several warrant article letters are garbled or not spoken clearly in the captions (e.g., the FY27 omnibus budget article, the FY27 capital budget article, and the SAP salary and vacation-buyout articles).

Full 5-count roll call is not audible for several votes, including the sewer enterprise fund (Z2), the free cash transfer to the OPEB trust fund, and the deferral of the Assistant Town Manager/HR Director article.
Exact dollar figures for the police cruiser line, the school door security intercom line, and the adult activity center network line are garbled ('68,627'/'418,627', '$24,44', '$20,45').
The prior-year Aeroseptic invoice amount '$57,77.50' is unclear as spoken and may be a mis-rendering of a different figure.
Some crosstalk during the health insurance stabilization fund and Assistant Town Manager discussions makes portions of the exchange between Anna and Jen hard to fully attribute.

what_happened.line: The committee put off recommending a position on the FY27 Proposition 2½ override until the full five-member board can meet.
It also deferred the FY27 omnibus town and school operating budget because final transfer figures were not yet ready.
A new special-purpose health insurance stabilization fund transfer passed its recommendation on a 4-1 vote.
A proposed Assistant Town Manager/HR Director grade change was pushed to the next meeting after members said it needed further discussion.
Most routine warrant articles -- revolving funds, the FY27 capital budget, and the water and solid waste enterprise funds -- were recommended for approval.

why_it_matters: The override recommendation touches what residents are asked to approve at town meeting or the ballot, and the committee is not yet on record with a position.
The FY27 omnibus budget funds town and school operations for the coming year; its numbers were not final at this meeting.
The health insurance stabilization fund is a new savings mechanism for a cost that affects both town and school budgets, and it did not pass without dissent.
watch_next: The next Finance Committee meeting, when the full board is expected to take up the override recommendation.
A future vote on the FY27 omnibus town/school budget article, once closeout and transfer figures are final.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on the mechanics of nearly every vote (motion, outcome, and any split count) once articles are matched up, but they diverge in two ways worth flagging: the official minutes record every dollar figure zero times (they give motion/seconder/roll-call only), so almost none of "ours" many dollar amounts can be checked against them, and there are several real vote-outcome conflicts — Article Q (300th anniversary) is unanimous in the official record but "4-1" in ours, Article P (compensated absence reserve) has a Jay Simeone nay the official record shows but ours omits, and two articles ours marked "not audible" (O, Z2) the official record shows were unanimously approved. A reader should check the actual warrant to resolve which SAP article (N vs. EE) corresponds to the "Assistant Town Manager/HR Director grade" item ours describes, since the two records' SAP-related outcomes don't cleanly line up.
